title: Echo Flight incident and the Boeing/SAC report

tellings.quote: The reason I think that it was actually UFO related is there was a Boeing uh uh strategic air command report where they actually looked and they tried to recreate the effect and this is on the Echolight incident.
>> uh Boeing also did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler.
tellings.difference: Names the logic coupler as the part bench-tested and credits James Klotz as a source.
tellings.link_reason: Boeing's bench test of the logic coupler is the Boeing/SAC attempt to recreate the Echo Flight effect that the host describes.

as_told.title: SAC documents show puzzlement and a Boeing investigation

plain: In 1967, nuclear missiles at a group of launch sites called Echo Flight, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, failed, and Michels says a report shows that something to do with UFOs was behind it. He describes a report by the aircraft and missile maker Boeing and the Strategic Air Command, the Air Force command in charge of nuclear bombers and missiles, in which they "tried to recreate the effect." Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who took part in the missile events of that period, says that "Boeing also did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler," a part in the missiles' electronics, and he credits a man named James Klotz for this. In another episode, Michels says the command's own papers show it was "extremely puzzled" and had "no idea what was going on." To them, the point is that the people who built and ran the missiles could not find an ordinary cause.
